cases.title: Profitable OEM instrument maker, temporary dip, leverage 2.1x, family stake 31%
reasons: No kill criteria met: Net debt/EBITDA is 2.1x (threshold 4x), no controlling shareholder has ruled out a sale (founding family at 31% has made no public statement either way), no regulatory issues reported.

cases.title: Profitable, cheap, but the market is going away
reasons: The price drop appears structural rather than temporary as required by the thesis criterion.
Revenue has fallen for three consecutive years with a 30% decline in the latest period, driven by the end of pandemic-era testing demand.
Management has disclosed no new products with meaningful sales to replace the lost market.
The loss of pandemic demand is a permanent structural market change, not a temporary product transition, destocking, or one-off charge as the thesis requires.
missing_facts: Whether the company has any strategic pivot or new market opportunities in development to address the structural loss of pandemic testing demand.
Percentage of sales from recurring revenue streams (consumables, service contracts) versus one-time test sales, to verify the business model criterion.

cases.title: The bad-fit example of the thesis: loss-making genomics lab
reasons: The company is outside the fund's target segments: genomic testing services is a test service business, not one of the specified segments (instruments, assays, OEM analyzers, lab automation). The thesis example explicitly cites 'a loss-making genomics lab whose growth depends on reimbursement decisions' as a bad fit, which describes GenoScope almost precisely.

The 55% price decline over 12 months combined with five years of consecutive losses suggests the decline may be structural rather than temporary. The thesis requires the price drop to be temporary (product transition, customer destocking, one-off charges), not a loss of market confidence.
The company's growth depends entirely on obtaining Medicare reimbursement for its main test, with the decision still pending. This creates unresolved business uncertainty.
missing_facts: Proportion of revenue from recurring sources (consumables, service contracts) versus one-time revenue—needed to assess the business model criterion

Evidence that the 55% price decline stems from a temporary factor (discrete product transition, one-time charge, temporary destocking) rather than from loss of confidence in a chronically unprofitable business model

cases.title: Clean fit whose FDA warning letter was formally closed three months ago
reasons: No kill criteria are met: net debt is 2.3x EBITDA (below the 4x threshold), there is no controlling shareholder (Norges Bank holds 6%), and the regulatory issue is formally resolved (FDA close-out letter received July 2026, shipments fully resumed).
The company operates in in-vitro diagnostics (molecular assays and instruments), which is within the target segments.
Recurring revenue from consumables and service is 72% of sales, exceeding the 50% threshold.
The 33% share price decline is temporary and now reversing: caused by the FDA warning letter on the main assay plant (2025) and shipment hold, both formally resolved by July 2026.

The company is profitable (21% EBITDA margin), has a strong balance sheet (2.3x leverage), and fits the fund's profile: a mid-sized diagnostics company whose share price fell for a temporary regulatory reason, now an opportunity to finance the next cycle away from quarterly pressure.
No controlling shareholder and no unresolved regulatory issues.

cases.title: Drop blamed on temporary destocking, but a major customer is also insourcing
reasons: The thesis requires the price drop to be temporary, but the facts show a structural component: a major customer (15% of sales) announced permanent migration to in-house platform from 2027.

While management attributes the profit warning to temporary customer destocking, the timing and magnitude of the customer loss suggests this may be the primary driver of the decline, not just a temporary setback.
Unknown: the relative contribution of temporary destocking vs. the announced permanent customer loss to the current profit warning and future revenue impact.

When will the customer loss materially hit revenue—is any part of it happening before 2027?
